newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Profit warning knocks IBM S.Africa further.
newsitem.headline: Profit warning knocks IBM S.Africa further.

text.p: IBM South Africa Ltd toppled to another new year low early on Wednesday afternoon after the company made a severe profit warning.
The share fell 180 cents to 11 rand. Volumes traded were fair with 13,500 shares changing hands by 1047 GMT. IBM was the fourth biggest percentage loser on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"It's hit by the profit warning. Pretty scary stuff and is down quite a bit," one dealer said.
The group announced earlier on Wednesday it expected to show a substantial trading loss for the six months' period ending June 30, 1997.
The computer firm also announced it would restructure to improve focus on higher growth areas in a bid to better its competitiveness.

Recently-appointed managing director Sal Faso said in a published announcement that in addition to the trading loss in the interim period, there will be further costs associated with the restructuring.
Dealers said earlier that it was likely IBM shares would take a further knock on Wednesday.
"We're likely to see quite a big shake-up there. It's going to be down some more," a dealer said.

IBM earnings for the year ended December 31, 1996 fell 27 percent to 73.8 million rand following the unsuccessful introduction of a new low-tier personal computer product. The product has been withdrawn.
